sentences.show: Two grenades landed in the trench. A 17-year-old Marine threw himself on both of them.
His name was Jack Lucas. And he had been lying about his age since he was fourteen.
In 1942, he forged his mother's signature, bribed a notary, and joined the Marines.
They kept him far from the fighting, in Hawaii. So he stowed away on a ship heading for Iwo Jima.
He turned himself in at sea, one day before he'd have been listed as a deserter. They handed him a rifle.
He turned 17 on the way. Five days later, he landed on Iwo Jima.
On the second day, he and three Marines dived into a trench, under enemy fire.
Two grenades landed at their feet.
Lucas shoved one into the volcanic ash, covered it with his body, and pulled the other one under him.
One exploded. The other never went off.
His three friends walked away without a scratch. They thought he was dead.
He wasn't. It took 21 operations, and about 200 pieces of metal stayed in his body for life.
They set off airport metal detectors for the rest of his life.
In October 1945, President Truman gave him the Medal of Honor. The youngest Marine to receive it in the war.
Years later, he became a paratrooper. On one jump, both his parachutes reportedly failed. He survived that too.
Jack never backed down. Don't scroll past the next one. Subscribe.
